subject: On-prem deployment: offline upgrades & hardware clarification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@medsys.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem deployment: offline upgrades & hardware clarification

Hi Anita —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Good high-level fit, and I wanted to capture the follow-ups we discussed so your procurement & infra teams can review. I added Vivek and Dylan from our solutions team.

Key items we need to qualify for our Private (on-prem / air-gapped) packaging and the next-stage proposal:

1) Hardware baseline: please confirm the target host spec you expect to run the inference cluster on (per-rack / per-node): CPU model, RAM, NVMe sizing, and exact GPU model/quantity per node (e.g., 4x A100-80GB, or 8x H100 80GB). If you have a preferred SKU we should validate against, attach it.

2) Network & air-gap: confirm whether the deployment will be fully air-gapped (no outbound) or whether you can allow a maintenance window with constrained egress for patch pulls. If fully air-gapped, we will provide offline upgrade bundles and a documented media-based upgrade procedure.

3) Upgrade cadence & acceptable downtime: what is your required quarterly/bi-annual upgrade cadence? What is the maximum maintenance window per cluster for upgrades (e.g., rolling upgrades with zero app-level downtime vs scheduled 2–4 hour windows)?

4) Key management & telemetry: do you require integration with an on-prem KMS/HSM? Can telemetry/health be routed to an internal monitoring endpoint, or do you need the system to operate without any telemetry leaving the network?

5) Maintenance ops: who will be the primary operator (title/team) for applying physical media and running offline upgrades? Do you have an internal runbook or do you want Redwood to include an operator runbook and remote training package?

Attachments: I included a short hardware spec sheet template (hw_spec_sheet.pdf) and a suggested procurement timeline (procurement_timeline.xlsx) to help your team consolidate answers.

Next steps: if you can reply with the fields above, we’ll draft a Private deployment proposal and a gallery of SKUs for the cluster (with pricing and a timeline for the on-prem package). If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute follow-up with your infra lead and our field engineer to walk the media-based upgrade flow.

Thanks — looking forward to the details.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@medsys.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medsys.io>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: offline upgrades & hardware clarification

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the attachments, that format is perfect. Answers inline below.

1) Hardware baseline: we are currently evaluating two SKUs internally: 4x A100-80GB, 2x Sapphire NVMs per node (512GB), 1.5TB RAM; and a higher-density option 8x H100-80GB with 2x NVMe 1TB, 2TB RAM. We expect procurement to lean toward the A100 nodes for cost reasons but would like to see validated performance numbers.

2) Network & air-gap: this will be an air-gapped installation at our primary datacenter for PHI workloads. No outbound connections allowed at rest. For upgrades, we are open to a controlled offline maintenance window where we can mount physical media or a temporary, isolated jump-host with tightly restricted egress (approval required).

3) Upgrade cadence & acceptable downtime: target cadence is quarterly security patches, major runtime upgrades once every 6–12 months. We require rolling upgrades where possible; a 3-hour scheduled maintenance window per cluster is acceptable for non-rolling operations. Zero-app-downtime is preferred but not mandatory.

4) Key management & telemetry: on-prem HSM (Thales) integration required for secrets. Telemetry must be optional and fully configurable; default must be disabled. Health checks should be exposed to our internal Prometheus stack only.

5) Maintenance ops: primary operator will be our Platform Engineering lead (Rajiv Mehta). He will run the physical-media upgrades. We would appreciate Redwood providing operator runbook, offline upgrade bundles, and a 2-hour training session for Rajiv and one backup engineer.

Attachments: I attached our procurement timeline grid and can share the formal hardware SKU once procurement has locked the PO.

Next: we’re aiming for a procurement decision by end of April. Please send a short on-prem proposal and a checklist for our infra team; we can then set a technical call with Rajiv next week.

Best,
Anita
Anita Shah
Head of Infrastructure | MedSys Health
anita.shah@medsys.io
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@medsys.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: offline upgrades & hardware clarification

Anita —

Appreciate the clear answers. Short notes from our side and proposed next steps: 

- Hardware: we’ll run a micro-benchmark on both the 4x A100 and 8x H100 configs (latency/throughput for your target sequence lengths) and include an expected tokens/sec table in the proposal. If you can share the final SKU we’ll validate the NVMe/PCI topology assumptions.

- Air-gap & upgrades: we’ll package an offline upgrade bundle and a prescriptive media-based upgrade playbook. For the HSM integration we support Thales and can provide the KMIP connector documentation. Telemetry will be configurable; default off.

- Runbook & training: we’ll include a 2-hour remote workshop and an operator runbook PDF in the proposal.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share a short Private deployment statement of work and a checklist for Rajiv by EOD today.
2) Can we put Rajiv and our field engineer (Dylan) on a 30-minute technical call next Tue 24 Mar at 10:00 PT? If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a pre-read (upgrade playbook stub).
3) I’ll attach the DocuSign preview for the Private package so procurement can see licensing & support terms.

I’ve attached the hardware template filled with what you sent (hw_spec_sheet.pdf) and the procurement timeline. If any of those dates shift, flag them back.

—
Marissa
